title: Customer Service Advisor - 12 month FTC
description:
As a Customer Care Coordinator in Warrington, you will handle customer enquiries and help keep day-to-day customer service running smoothly within the Not For Profit sector. You will provide clear updates, resolve queries where possible and make sure customers receive a helpful and consistent service.

Client Details

The organisation operates in the Housing Sector in Warrington

Description
- Respond to customer enquiries by phone, email and other agreed channels, giving clear and accurate information.
- Record customer contacts and update relevant systems to keep information complete and easy to follow.
- Resolve straightforward issues promptly and pass more complex queries to the appropriate colleague.
- Keep customers informed about the progress of their enquiry, helping to provide a reliable service.
- Handle complaints in a calm and professional way, ensuring details are recorded accurately.
- Work with colleagues across Customer Service to coordinate responses and avoid unnecessary delays.
- Maintain organised records of customer interactions to support effective follow-up.
- Identify recurring customer queries and share feedback to help improve the customer experience.

Profile

A successful 'Customer Care Coordinator' should have:
- Experience of handling customer enquiries and providing clear, helpful responses.
- Confidence using phone and email communication to manage customer contact.
- The ability to record information accurately and keep customer records up to date.
- Experience of resolving queries and recognising when an issue needs to be escalated.
- A practical approach to managing several customer contacts while maintaining service standards.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.

Job Offer
- Fixed-term contract.
- Salary up to 27,982 dependent on the level of experience.
- Customer Care Coordinator role based in Warrington

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

As an inclusive recruiter we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and experiences. If you require any adjustments or accommodations during the recruitment process, we'll work with you to ensure you can perform at your best.

title: Scheduling Administrator

- Monday to Friday

- Office Administration: 1 year (required)

title: Office Admin - St. Helens Secondary
description:

This role is initially focused on document digitisation and improving filing systems, but there is potential for wider administrative responsibilities as needs evolve. The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring efficient record-keeping and contributing to a well-run school office.

Essential:

title: Operations Administrator
description:
Operations Administrator
- Competitive Salary
- Full-time, Permanent
- St Helens, WA9 5 GZ

Ready to play a key role in keeping nationwide distribution operations moving?

Streetwise Distribution is looking for a proactive, organised and confident Operations Administrator to join our team at our St Helens hub.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys communicating with people and has a natural talent for keeping things organised. You'll be at the heart of our daily operations, helping coordinate publication and leaflet distribution campaigns across our nationwide delivery network.

Working alongside office colleagues, field teams, supervisors and external delivery partners, you'll help ensure campaigns run smoothly, information is accurate and any challenges are dealt with quickly and effectively.

If you're an excellent communicator, confident with IT and someone who enjoys taking ownership, solving problems and getting things done, we'd love to hear from you!

What will you be doing?

Your responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating the day-to-day delivery of publication and leaflet distribution campaigns from our St Helens hub.
- Building and maintaining strong relationships with our nationwide network of field teams, supervisors and delivery partners.
- Preparing accurate delivery instructions, schedules, area allocations and operational records.
- Keeping track of campaign progress, chasing updates and resolving delivery queries or issues.
- Using Microsoft Excel, Outlook, Word, Teams and internal systems to manage information and produce reports.
- Supporting operational reporting, including delivery updates, coverage information and performance data.
- Assisting with stock movements and palletised consignments when required.
- Spotting potential issues, finding practical solutions and helping us continually improve how we work.
- Supporting the wider operations team during busy periods.

What we're looking for

You'll ideally have:
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel, Outlook, Word and Teams.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- A proactive, can-do attitude and a practical approach to problem-solving.
- Confidence communicating with people at all levels, both internally and externally.
- Great attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
- The ability to work independently while being a supportive team player.

Experience in logistics, distribution, fulfilment or campaign coordination would be an advantage, but it's not essential. We'll provide full training for the right person.

What you'll get in return
- A full-time, permanent position within a growing distribution business.
- A varied role where your contribution really matters.
- The opportunity to take on responsibility and develop your skills.
- A friendly, supportive team environment.
- The chance to be part of a business delivering campaigns nationwide.

Ready to join the team?

If you're an organised people-person who enjoys a challenge and wants to build a career in distribution operations, we want to hear from you.

title: Part Time Administrator
description:
Part-Time Administrator

Location: Haydock
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9.15am 3.00pm
Pay: £14.10 per hour
Job Type: Part-time, permanent

- Option to buy an additional 5 days' holiday from day one
- Private medical cover from day one
- Permanent position
- Monday to Friday, 9.15am 3:00pm
- 37.5 hours per week

About The Role

Teleios Recruitment is recruiting for an established Fire & Security business based in Haydock.

The company provides Fire & Security services to a wide range of commercial clients, with a busy service and maintenance operation covering areas including fire alarms, CCTV, intruder alarms, access control and emergency lighting.

We are looking for a Part-Time Administrator to join the team. This is a heavily data input and job administration role where accuracy is absolutely essential.

When a job comes into the business, you will be responsible for making sure the information is entered correctly and that the job is logged and updated across the relevant systems, depending on the type of work.

You will also be responsible for adding job sheets and paperwork, keeping records up to date and making sure information is accurate throughout the life of each job.

Key Responsibilities
- Logging new jobs onto Salesforce and the relevant internal systems
- Entering accurate job and customer information
- Adding and uploading completed job sheets and paperwork
- Updating job records as work progresses
- Ensuring information is entered onto the correct system depending on the type of job, including maintenance and security work
- Checking information carefully and identifying any errors
- Keeping records and spreadsheets up to date
- Matching completed paperwork to the relevant jobs
- Following up outstanding paperwork and information
- Providing updates on live jobs where required
- General administration and high-volume data input
- Working closely with engineers, service managers and the wider team

Essential Criteria
- Previous administration and data input experience
- Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy
- Confident using computer systems and entering large amounts of information
- Good Excel skills
- Previous experience within the Fire & Security industry is highly desirable
- Comfortable working with job sheets, service records and technical paperwork
- Good telephone manner
- Able to work independently and manage your own workload
- Reliable with good attendance
- Organised and methodical
- A good team player

The most important part of this role is accuracy. You will be dealing with a high volume of information and multiple jobs, so we need someone who is methodical, organised and takes the time to check their work carefully.

Previous experience within Fire & Security would be a real advantage, as an understanding of the industry and the different types of jobs coming into the business will help you settle into the role quickly.

title: Credit Control & Contracts Coordinator
description:
Credit Control & Contracts Coordinator
- Kirkby, Liverpool
- Salary - 29,000 - 31,000 per annum
- Full time - Monday to Friday, 8:45am - 5pm
- Permanent
- Holidays - 25 days + bank holidays + birthday off!

Are you an experienced Credit Controller looking for a role where you can make a genuine impact beyond the traditional finance function?

We're recruiting on behalf of a growing and established business in Liverpool seeking a Credit Control & Contracts Coordinator to join their team. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with strong credit control experience who also enjoys improving processes, building systems and working closely with stakeholders across a business.

The role is approximately 60% credit control and 40% contracts administration, with the emphasis very much on finding someone who can confidently take ownership of credit control responsibilities from day one.

The Opportunity

You'll be responsible for managing customer debt, maintaining healthy cash flow and resolving payment queries, whilst also playing a key role in introducing a more structured and centralised approach to contract administration.

This isn't a legal or commercial contracts position. Instead, you'll take ownership of organising, tracking and maintaining important company agreements, ensuring key dates, renewals and documentation are properly managed and never missed.

If you enjoy bringing order to complex information, creating efficient processes and seeing projects through to completion, this could be the ideal next step.

Key Responsibilities

Credit Control
- Managing outstanding customer accounts and aged debt.
- Chasing overdue payments and maintaining regular customer contact.
- Investigating and resolving invoice and payment queries.
- Liaising with internal departments to resolve account issues.
- Supporting account reconciliations and maintaining accurate records.
- Prioritising and managing your own workload effectively.

Contracts Administration
- Building and maintaining a central contracts register.
- Gathering and organising agreements from across the business.
- Recording key contractual information including renewal dates, notice periods and contract ownership.
- Identifying missing, expired or incomplete agreements.
- Coordinating contract renewals and reviews.
- Following up with managers and stakeholders to ensure actions are completed.
- Establishing robust systems and processes to keep contract information accurate and up to date.

What We're Looking For
- Previous hands-on Credit Control experience
- Strong administration and organisational skills
- Good Excel and data management skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- Confident communication skills
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently
- Proactive and solutions-focused approach

If you're looking for a position where you can utilise your credit control expertise whilst taking on broader business responsibilities, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today or contact us for a confidential discussion.

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

title: Administrator
company: North Cheshire and Mersey NHS Foundation Trust (BCH)
advertiser_name: North Cheshire and Mersey NHS Foundation Trust (BCH)
description: The Administrator will provide administrative support to the Drive Ability North West (DANW) service, ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of the departments administrative processes. This varied and busy role is central to the service, acting as a key point of contact for patients, carers, colleagues, partner agencies and stakeholders. The successful candidate will communicate professionally and confidently with a wide range of people, including those who may have communication difficulties. They will answer telephone calls, respond to enquiries in person, telephone and by email, and take appropriate action or redirect queries where necessary. Reception cover will be part of the role, as required, by the service. Accuracy and organisation are essential. The post holder will undertake data entry, maintain electronic and paper records, prepare and produce documents, and ensure information is kept correct and up to date in line with Trust policy. They will also be responsible for arranging and booking Blue Badge assessment clinics, helping the service to make the best use of available appointments. The role requires confident use of DANW and Warrington Council IT systems, including email, to receive and pass on information efficiently. The post holder will work closely with the Operational Manager, Team Lead, Clinicians and the Administrator staff, contributing to the smooth running of assessment services. The post holder will provide comprehensive administrative support and will act as the first point of contact for all patient and carer enquiries. They will deal with telephone and face-to-face enquiries efficiently and professionally, taking action or redirecting calls as appropriate and will liaise with internal and external services and partner agencies as directed. Central to the role is maintaining the patient booking system. This includes entering referrals onto the database, preparing and arranging appointments, sending appointment letters, and ensuring all clerical work is completed in a prompt and accurate manner. The post holder will keep the DANW diary and Blue Badge clinics booked to full capacity in line with the agreed processes. They will cancel and rebook patients, when necessary and will maintain and update waiting lists and clinical diaries as requested. Record keeping is a key responsibility. The post holder will ensure all electronic and paper records are accurate and up to date, file general documentation and clinical records correctly, manage photocopying, filing and archiving in line with Trust policy. They will also contribute to departmental audit activity and collect data and statistics for staff and managers. Please see Full Job Description attached. The post holder will provide an effective and efficient administrative support service to the Drive Ability North West (DANW) Team Lead and assessment team, ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of administrative processes. Duties will include communicating professionally and effectively with staff, patients and other departments; answering telephone calls and responding to enquiries; undertaking accurate data entry and maintaining records; preparing and producing documents; providing reception cover as required; and arranging and booking Blue Badge assessment clinics. . Duties and Responsibilities The following are an example of the duties the post holder many undertake. Training and support will be provided: Provide a comprehensive administration support service to include typing of a range of documents Receives and deals with telephone calls for the department and taking appropriate action when necessary To act as first point of contact for all patient and carer enquiries, responding to telephone and face to face enquiries in an efficient, tactful and professional manner, redirecting calls, taking action as appropriate. Liaising with internal and external services and partner agencies when necessary as directed To have excellent communication skills and the confidence and skills to talk to people who may have communication difficulties Ensure that all departmental electronic and paper records are correct and up to date, including accurate filing of general documentation and results if (clinical based) Opening, sorting, distribution and dispatch of post Use of all DANW systems, Trust information and computer systems for day-to-day processes e.g. e-mails to receive and pass on information. Deal with enquiries from clients, relatives and other health professionals in a courteous and professional manner To carry out general office duties where required, maintaining a tidy office environment Maintain and update waiting lists The maintenance of the patient booking system to include the preparation and arrangement of appointments, including inputting of referrals onto the database and sending appointment letters, ensuring all clerical work is dealt with in a timely manner Ensure DANW diary and Blue Badge clinics booked to full capacity as per the agreed template. Make suggestions as to any modification to ensure smooth running of clinic based on demand. Cancelling and re-booking patients who have had to be cancelled, due to, for example, sickness of clinician Collect relevant data / statistics as requested by staff/managers To carry out case note audits To contribute to departments audit activity To accept deliveries and ensure these are dealt with promptly; To maintain an effective photocopying, filing and archiving system including records management in line with Trust policy
